key_idea: Flat faces are ruled out by defining an infimal period excess b(n) over a class of local randomized 'roads' along the face directions, then showing it is bounded below by a positive constant but also contracts geometrically under scale changes (b(Dn) ≤ ρ b(n)); corners are ruled out separately with multiscale characteristic lengths and a BK disjoint-witness counting argument.
reason: The final contradiction, a quantity that is bounded below by a positive constant yet contracts geometrically, is short and clear. Reaching it takes more than fifty lemmas: calibrations, local gauges, finite-cell potentials, lattice permutations, charged tunnels, truncations and road surgery. That bookkeeping hides why exponential or Gamma weights should force strict convexity and smoothness, and the corner and face arguments are two separate heavy machines instead of one idea.
